q: 1. For covering sheds required in chemical industries, the sheets used are made of
explain: Asbestos cement sheets resist chemical attack and weathering, making them suitable for chemical industry sheds.

q: 2. A hydro-carbon material that completely soluble in carbon disulphide is known as
explain: Bitumen is a hydrocarbon material that is completely soluble in carbon disulphide, a key test for its purity/identification.

q: 3. The colour of asphalt is
options: deep black with slight tinge of redness
explain: Asphalt is generally described as black-brownish in color, distinguishing it visually from other bituminous materials.

q: 4. Coal-tar is obtained by destructive distillation of
explain: Coal-tar is a byproduct obtained from the destructive (high-temperature, air-free) distillation of coal.

q: 5. Bitumen felt is used for
explain: Bitumen felt is impermeable and flexible, making it ideal for waterproofing and damp-proofing applications.

q: 6. Enamel paint is made by adding
explain: Enamel paint is produced by adding white lead pigment to varnish, giving a hard, glossy, durable finish.

q: 7. In paints, pigment is responsible for .....
explain: Pigments give paint its colour.

q: 8. Asbestos is a good insulator of
explain: Asbestos is a versatile insulator against heat, sound, and electricity due to its fibrous, non-conductive structure.

q: 9. The chief ingredient of a paint is .....
explain: Pigment is the chief ingredient, giving colour and body to the paint.

q: 10. Chemically asbestos is composed of
explain: Asbestos is chemically a calcium magnesium silicate, represented as CaSiO3.3MgSiO3.

q: 11. The liquid medium used in oil paints is .....
explain: Linseed oil is the liquid medium (vehicle) of oil paints.

q: 12. The melting point of asbestos is
explain: Asbestos fibers typically melt/decompose in the range of about 1200°C to 1500°C.

q: 13. The pigment in paints is mixed to give desired .....
explain: Pigment is added to give the desired colour.

q: 14. Asbestos is not affected by
explain: Asbestos is chemically inert and resistant to acids, alkalies, and corrosion, contributing to its wide industrial use.

q: 15. The liquid part of the paint is called .....
explain: The liquid part (usually oil) that carries the pigment is the vehicle.

q: 16. The standard width of asbestos cement sheet is
explain: Standard asbestos cement corrugated sheets are commonly manufactured with a width of about 1.23 m.

q: 17. The liquid medium used in enamel paints is .....
explain: Enamel paint is made by mixing pigment (white lead or zinc white) in varnish.

q: 18. A hydro-carbon material of either natural or pyrogenous origin, and completely soluble in carbon disulphide is known as
explain: Bitumen, whether of natural or refinery (pyrogenous) origin, is defined by its complete solubility in carbon disulphide.

q: 19. The metallic oxide used in the form of powder in a paint is called .....
explain: The base is a metallic oxide in powder form, such as white lead, zinc oxide or titanium white.

q: 20. ...... tar is produced by distillation of bituminous shales.
explain: Mineral tar is produced specifically from the distillation of bituminous shale rock.

q: 21. The base in a paint is added to .....
options: hide the surface to be painted
explain: As per the answer key, the base gives the paint body and opacity so it hides the surface to be painted.

q: 22. Asphalt is a
options: mixture of bitumen and inert material
explain: Asphalt is essentially a mixture of bitumen combined with inert mineral matter (sand, limestone, etc.).

q: 23. The commonly base used in a paint is .....
explain: Any of these can be used as a paint base.

q: 24. Asphalt is a good insulator of
explain: Asphalt, being a dense hydrocarbon-mineral composite, insulates well against heat, sound, and electrical conduction.

q: 25. The thinner used for oil paints is .....
explain: Turpentine is the usual thinner for oil paints; water does not mix with oil.

q: 26. Regarding solubility of asphalt, it is soluble in
explain: Since asphalt contains inert mineral matter along with bitumen, it dissolves only partially in carbon disulphide, unlike pure bitumen.

q: 27. Linseed oil in paint is used as a .....
explain: Linseed oil acts as the carrier of pigment and dries to form a film.

q: 28. The specific gravity of bitumen is
explain: Bitumen typically has a specific gravity of around 1.0 to 1.09, slightly denser than water.

q: 29. Linseed oil is rapidly soluble in .....
explain: As per the answer key, all of these. Linseed oil is soluble in turpentine and naphtha, and the key accepts alcohol too.

q: 30. Coal-tar is obtained by destructive distillation of
explain: Coal-tar results from the destructive distillation of coal, a byproduct of coke and gas production.

q: 31. The commonly used extender in a paint is .....
explain: As per the answer key, any one of these. Barium sulphate and gypsum are extenders, and alcohol is included in the book's key answer.

q: 32. Cutbacks are used
explain: Cutback bitumen is thinned with a volatile solvent so it can be applied without needing to be heated.

q: 33. The drier in an oil paint should not be more than ..... (by volume).
explain: As per the answer key, driers should not exceed 10% by volume.

q: 34. Glass marker soap is added in suitable proportion to correct the colour of glass due to the presence of iron in raw materials of glass and is chemically known as
explain: Cadmium sulphate ('glass maker's soap') is added to counteract the greenish tint caused by iron impurities in raw glass materials.

q: 35. The commonly used solvent in oil paints is .....
explain: Turpentine or naphtha can be used as the solvent.

q: 36. The melting temperature of ordinary glass is
explain: Ordinary soda-lime glass melts in the range of approximately 1400°C to 1500°C.

q: 37. The co-efficient of expansion of glass is
explain: Ordinary glass has a relatively high coefficient of thermal expansion, which is why it can crack under sudden temperature changes.

q: 38. For providing windscreen of cars, buses and other automobile vehicles, the glass used is
explain: Laminated glass, with a plastic interlayer, holds together on impact and is used for automobile windscreens for safety.

q: 39. Glass wool has low
explain: Glass wool's fibrous, air-trapping structure gives it low heat conductivity, making it an effective thermal insulator.

q: 40. Which of the following material exhibits plasticity?
explain: Copper, steel, and hot bitumen can all be deformed and reshaped without breaking, exhibiting plasticity under appropriate conditions.

q: 41. In paints, pigment is responsible for:
explain: Pigment is the solid coloring component in paint responsible for its color and opacity.

q: 42. Asphalt is a
options: mixture of bitumen and inert material
explain: Asphalt is a mixture of bitumen with inert mineral matter such as sand or limestone dust.

q: 43. The filler used in plastic bitumen, is .....
explain: As per the answer key, asbestos powder is used as the filler. (The book prints 'tale' for talc in option b.)

q: 44. French polish is a kind of
explain: French polish is a type of spirit varnish made by dissolving shellac in alcohol/spirit.

q: 45. Paints with white lead base are suitable for painting of
options: both wood work and iron work
explain: White lead based paints are best suited for wood work, as they adhere well and protect timber surfaces effectively.

q: 46. Duco paint is
explain: Duco is a well-known brand of cellulose (nitrocellulose) paint, known for its quick drying and glossy finish.

q: 47. Linseed oil is rapidly soluble in
explain: Linseed oil readily dissolves in a range of common solvents including turpentine, naphtha, and alcohol.

q: 48. Lithophone is
options: an oxide of iron used as a base
explain: Lithopone is a white pigment composed of zinc sulfide and barium sulfate, used as an alternative to white lead.

q: 49. When liquid asphalt is dissolved in a volatile solvent such as naptha or benzole we get
explain: Dissolving asphalt in a volatile solvent like naphtha produces cutback asphalt, which can be applied without heating.

q: 50. The basic purpose of a retarder in concrete is
options: to increase the initial setting time of cement paste in concrete
to decrease the initial setting time of cement paste in concrete
to render the concrete more water tight
to improve the workability of concrete mix
explain: A retarder is added specifically to extend (increase) the initial setting time, giving more working time before the concrete sets.
